failure_summary.description: Agents used an over-specific label or a nearby retrieval detail instead of following the clue's requested answer level or explicit referent.
Granularity and completion rules were too categorical, encouraging agents to omit words that are integral to a canonical name or title.
The expected answer conflicted with the clue, the prompt lacked a clear answer slot, or the gold answer was broader than the context-supported answer.

patch.reasoning: The evidence-check and requested-slot rules already address the retrieval and clue-selection errors, so they need no duplication. The recurring patchable issue is that concise-answer and blank-completion guidance can remove integral parts of canonical names; qualify both rules while preserving their usual preference for concise answers.

edits.target: - Give the shortest unambiguous answer at the requested granularity. When the context supplies a concise answer label, use that form rather than expanding it into a fuller name, title, or role description merely because the expansion is also correct. When a category is already specified in the question, provide the distinguishing value rather than repeating the category.
edits.content: - Give the shortest unambiguous answer at the requested granularity. When the context supplies a concise answer label, use it rather than adding merely descriptive expansions. When a category is already specified, normally give the distinguishing value rather than restating the category; however, retain a category-like word when it is integral to the context-supported canonical proper name or title.

edits.target: - For completion or compound clues, identify the missing shared component that makes the alternatives fit; do not repeat a clue-supplied component or return one full compound.
edits.content: - For completion or compound clues, normally provide only the missing component. If the clue is asking for an established proper name, title, or other named entity, give its context-supported canonical full form when that is the requested referent, even if the clue supplies one component. For alternatives that share a component, provide the shared component rather than one full alternative.
